PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. FOR QUESTIONS OR ASSISTANCE, PLEASE CONTACT THE CITY CLERK'S OFFICE AT 949-724-6205, OR VIA EMAIL AT CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG. LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  May 11, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 5:10 p.m. on May
11, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout
City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to submit live
comments via Zoom and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
on all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded
to the City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  May 11, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commander Noelle Smiley introduced the Irvine Police Color Guard and led the Pledge
  of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Frank Winans from Woodbridge Community Church provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Proclaim May 9-15, 2021, as “National Police Week”

  Mayor Khan introduced Police Officers Gavin Hudson and Pat Ryan,
  and presented a proclamation recognizing May 9-15, 2021, as “National
  Police Week.”

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proclamation:

  •  Stephen Coffey, Irvine resident
  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Chelsea Boyle, Irvine resident

  1.2  Proclaim May 18, 2021, as “Asian American and Pacific Islander Day
  Against Bullying and Hate”

  Mayor Khan presented a proclamation recognizing May 18, 2021, as
  “Asian American and Pacific Islander Day Against Bullying and Hate.”

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Kim presented a video by the Racial Equality Club at Woodbridge High
  School, and suggested contacting club representatives for those interested in learning
  more about the club or planting an equality tree at a school or business.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  May 11, 2021

  Councilmember Agran referenced correspondence from Attorney Kevin Shenkman
  with the Southwest Voter Project, which alleged that the City was in violation of the
  California Voting Rights Act as the current at-large voting system discriminated against
  racial and ethnic minorities; and further noted that while he agreed with the City
  Attorney that the City could win a potential lawsuit, he suggested consideration of
  enlarging the City Council to seven seats and moving to voting districts. He also noted
  that he would be seeking City Council support to place the item on an upcoming agenda
  for City Council and community discussion.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  Last month, the City opened a drive-thru vaccination clinic at the Orange County
  Great Park in partnership with Providence Health System. The clinic is open
  Monday through Friday from 8 to 11:30 a.m. in Parking Lot 2. Both Moderna and
  Johnson & Johnson vaccines are being administered at the vaccination site.
  Appointments can be made at myturn.ca.gov or by calling 833-422-4255. For
  information, visit cityofirvine.org/vaccine.

  •  The City is excited to announce the launch of the 50th Anniversary Photo Contest.
  Community members are invited to submit their best photos of Irvine in the
  following categories:

  o  Cultural and Community
  o  Historical
  o  Outdoors
  o  Pets
  o  Submissions from those 17 and under

  Winners in each category will be revealed in the winter issue of Inside Irvine and
  featured in an exhibition at the Irvine Civic Center. A grand prize winner will
  receive a $250 gift card to the Irvine Spectrum Center. Submissions will be
  accepted through August 31. For more information, including official contest rules
  and entry guidelines, visit cityofirvine.org.

  •  The City’s traditional Memorial Day events have been modified this year to allow
  the community to honor fallen service members while still maintaining health and
  safety precautions. The Northwood Memorial Candle Lighting will take place over
  two days. Community members are encouraged to visit the memorial on
  Saturday, May 29, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. and on Sunday, May 30, from noon to 8
  p.m. to pay their respects to the fallen. Staff will be on-site to assist and ensure
  social distancing and gathering guidelines are being maintained. On Monday,
  May 31, at 10 a.m., the annual Memorial Day Ceremony will be presented online.
  A pre-recorded video presentation featuring tributes to military fallen by
  commanding officers from Irvine’s adopted 2/11 Marine Battalion and
  presentations from former ceremonies will be available online at cityofirvine.org.
  For more information, please call 949-724-6606.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  May 11, 2021

  •  On May 22, the community is invited to participate in Love Irvine’s first Citywide
  Serve Day, which provides an opportunity for the entire community to work
  together to serve and make a difference by participating in a beautification project
  along the Jeffrey Open Space Trail. Participants will be picking up litter along the
  trail from 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. and can meet at the Trabuco Center, where gloves
  and trash bags will be provided. For more information and to register, visit
  cityofirvine.org or loveirvine.org.

  Mayor Khan also invited Pastor Jason Aguilar from Arise Church Irvine to provide
  additional information on the Love Irvine initiative.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Kim, seconded by Councilmember Carroll,
  and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1
  through 2.3, and 2.5 through 2.7. Consent Calendar Item No. 2.4 was
  removed for separate discussion.

  2.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of the special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on April 13, 2021.
  2) Approved the minutes of the regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on April 13, 2021.

  2.2  PROCLAMATIONS

  Prior to approval of the Consent Calendar, 949-***-*366 and Nissreen
  spoke in support of Food Allergy Awareness Week.

  1) Ratified and Proclaimed April 30, 2021, as "Arbor Day."
  2) Proclaimed May 9-15, 2021, as "Food Allergy Awareness
  Week."
  3) Proclaimed May 2021 as "Mental Health Awareness Month."

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  May 11, 2021

  2.3  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-23 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND
  SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO
  BE PAID

  2.4  CONTRACT BUDGET APPROPRIATION FOR DEMOLITION AT
  1851 KETTERING

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of
  Councilmember Kuo, who inquired about the time sensitivity of the
  abatement and public nuisance that was originally approved by the City
  Council in June 2020.

  Keri Bullock, Neighborhood Services Administrator, and Pete
  Carmichael, Director of Community Development, responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included: questioning delays related to
  demolition; inquired about the lien process and remedies available if
  funds for demolition were not reimbursed by the property owner;
  questioned the differences between the Kettering property and a former
  residential public nuisance (“Castle House”); expressed concerns about
  the delay in demolition based on City Council approval in June 2020;
  inquired about the authority granted for a 30-day extension; and
  questioned whether estimated construction costs included any
  abatement of hazardous materials.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that a nuisance abatement situation
  provides the City with the ability to place an assessment on the property
  and collect the amount of fees owed; and that while the Castle House
  experience was similar, the City moved the building into receivership,
  which enabled a third-party custodian to take responsibility for
  remediating the property and collecting fees against the property owner.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Mayor
  Khan, and unanimously carried to:

  1) Approve a budget adjustment appropriating funds in the
  amount of $565,358 from the Asset Management Fund.
  2) Authorize staff to negotiate and award a contract for the
  necessary work for the demolition at 1851 Kettering in
  accordance with the City's procurement and competitive
  bidding procedures.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  May 11, 2021

  2.5  ACCEPTANCE OF HIGHWAY SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM
  GRANT FUNDS

  ACTION:
  1) Authorized the Director of Public Works and Transportation to
  approve and accept a Highway Safety Improvement Program
  Grant to Prepare a Local Roadway Safety Plan in the amount
  of $72,000.
  2) Authorized the Director of Public Works and Transportation to
  approve and accept a Highway Safety Improvement Program
  Grant to construct pedestrian improvements in the amount of
  $248,162.
  3) Approved a budget adjustment in the amount of $320,162
  reflecting an increase in revenues and appropriations and
  establish a Capital Improvement Project to construct pedestrian
  improvements in the amount of $291,400.

  2.6  COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP FUND GRANT NOMINATIONS

  Prior to approval of the Consent Calendar, the following spoke in
  opposition to Community Partnership Fund Grant Nomination funding
  for Team Kids, Inc.:

  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Stephen Coffey, Irvine resident

  Justin Fong, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition to Community
  Partnership Fund Grant Nomination funding for Team Kids, Inc. and
  Crime Survivors.

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, spoke in support of Community
  Partnership Fund Grant Nomination funding for Team Kids, Inc.

  Approved Mayor Khan's request for Community Partnership Fund
  Grant Nominations to the following organizations in support of
  program costs:

  a) Human Options ($500)
  b) South County Outreach ($500)
  c) Working Wardrobes ($500)
  d) Crime Survivors ($500)
  e) Orange County Asian and Pacific Islander Community
  Alliance ($500)
  f) Team Kids, Inc. ($500)
  g) Assistance League of Irvine ($500)

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6

  2.7  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 21-05 -

  UNBUILT RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS FROM PLANNING
  AREAS 9 (WOODBURY) AND 40 (CYPRESS VILLAGE) TO

  3.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  3.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE; PROPOSED REOPENING

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager, and Pamela Baird,
  Director of Community Services, presented the staff report and
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about the Global Village
  Festival and the potential for in-person attendance; and suggested that

  Hgo, Irvine resident, spoke in support of re-opening the Turtle Rock

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, spoke in support of continuing the
  summer drive-in movies and concerts at the Orange County Great

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded  by
  Councilmember Carroll, and unanimously carried to:

  Extend all previously issued City orders and resolutions related to

  3.2  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY VICE MAYOR KIM, CO-
  SPONSORED BY MAYOR KHAN, TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION
  URGING THE ORANGE COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS TO
  HOLD A PUBLIC MEETING CONCERNING THE EXPANSION OF
  THE JAMES A. MUSICK JAIL FACILITY

  This item was agendized at the request of Vice Mayor Kim, and co-
  sponsored by Mayor Khan, who requested City Council consideration
  of adoption of a resolution urging the Orange County Board of
  Supervisors to hold a public meeting concerning the expansion of the
  James A. Musick Jail Facility.

  City Council discussion included: noting multiple attempts by the City in
  the past opposing the expansion; expressed concern about language
  within the resolution with respect to the County not holding a public
  forum; suggested minor modifications within the proposed resolution;
  and suggested that the resolution be conveyed to the Orange County
  Board of Supervisors in the strongest terms to prevent further delays.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the proposed resolution:

  •  Jacob Reisberg
  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
